newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Avonmore/Waterford urge merger.
newsitem.headline: Avonmore/Waterford urge merger.

text.p: The chairmen of Avonmore Foods and Waterford Foods Plc urged members of the two Co-operatives on Monday to back merger proposals at meetings this month which would creat a food giant.
John Dowley, Waterford's chairman, and John Duggan, his counterpart at Avonmore, said the merger would create one of the largest dairy groups in the world.

"Creating a farmer-controlled organisation capable of competing in local and international markets is essential to ensure abover average returns to our farmers into the next century," their letter said.

"The enlarged operation, which wil be one of the largest dairy groups in the world, will be in a strong position to face up to the enormous change and challenge currently taking place in the food sector worldwide," the letter said.
"In essence, the benefits of merging our two businesses far outweigh any other option."
The first special general meeting of the Co-ops will be held simultaneously in Kilkenny and Waterford on Friday July 11. A second round of meetings wil be held on July 25.
A 75 percent majority of those present and voting at each meeting is required to approve the merger.
Waterford said on May 27 that it had agreed an improved 337 million irish pound offer from Avonmore, which would be put to Co-operative members and shareholders for agreement.
If the merger goes ahead, it will weld together two of Ireland's premier food companies and create the largest dairy company in Britain and Ireland and the fourth largest milk processor in the world.
